questions.title: Disaster and population needs
questions.question: What disaster effects and affected populations are reported for CORAL TEMPEST?
questions.expected_answer: Category-5 Cyclone RUA struck Efate on 5 February, severely damaging Port Vila, Bauerfield and Lapetasi. Water, power and fixed communications on Efate are largely inoperative. Displacement is reported on Efate, the Shepherd Islands and parts of Espiritu Santo, with incomplete casualty/displacement totals and acute water, medical and shelter needs.

criteria.text: Identifies Category-5 Cyclone RUA as the event.
Identifies damage to Port Vila/Bauerfield/Lapetasi.
Identifies loss of water services.
Identifies power loss.
Identifies loss of fixed communications.
Identifies Efate as affected.
Identifies the Shepherd Islands as affected.
Identifies parts of Espiritu Santo as affected.
Preserves incomplete casualty/displacement totals.
Identifies acute water, medical and shelter needs as reported.

acceptable_alternatives: A needs-and-effects table is acceptable.
error_conditions: Invents population totals or implies every island is equally affected.
questions.derivation_note: Retrieves the supplied scenario statement with its qualifications.

questions.title: Entry points and distribution limits
questions.question: What condition and distribution constraints are reported for the main air and sea entry points?
questions.expected_answer: Bauerfield has degraded airfield/terminal/navigation infrastructure with constrained ramp and handling capacity. Lapetasi is partially blocked and structurally degraded pending survey/clearance. Santo-Pekoa is less affected and offers a northern aerial alternative. Luganville wharf is intact and can berth large ships, but use is politically contested. Arrival at any entry point is separate from delivery to outer islands, which needs rotary-wing or small-craft movement.

criteria.text: States the Bauerfield operating constraints.
States the Lapetasi operating constraints.
Identifies less-affected Santo-Pekoa as a northern alternate.
Identifies intact but contested Luganville wharf.
Distinguishes entry-point arrival from onward distribution.

acceptable_alternatives: Group air and sea alternatives in a table.
error_conditions: Assumes intact infrastructure is approved for use.
Equates landing cargo with delivery to affected communities.
questions.derivation_note: Retrieves the supplied scenario statement with its qualifications.

questions.title: Sea-based support and closure
questions.question: What sea-based and other support is apportioned, and what is its availability status?
questions.expected_answer: Planning apportionment includes a JTF headquarters, an amphibious/sea-based component with rotary/tilt-wing lift, landing craft, medical and over-the-shore logistics, plus airlift and engineer/medical/logistics elements. These assets close over time; strategic lift, sealift and ISR are shared. Sea-based and over-the-shore delivery are supplied alternatives to degraded ports, not confirmed fully available capability at start.

criteria.text: Identifies the main apportioned support categories.
Identifies sea-based connectors and over-the-shore capability.
States that support is shared against theater priorities.
States time-phased force closure.

acceptable_alternatives: Capability categories suffice without unit designators.
error_conditions: Treats all apportioned assets as immediately on scene.
questions.derivation_note: Construction-stage correction for R032. Sea-basing/over-the-shore delivery is already explicitly supplied and is used as A, with a separate derived compatibility/readiness consequence.

questions.title: End-to-end relief feasibility
questions.question: What determines whether a large arrival of relief cargo would translate into usable relief for dispersed outer-island populations?
questions.expected_answer: Usable delivery depends on the whole path, including entry-point handling, onward connectors, landing/offload conditions and local receipt/distribution. Large upstream stocks or shipping capacity can exceed the constrained downstream segment. Sea-basing reduces fixed-port dependence but still requires compatible ship-to-shore and local distribution capacity.

criteria.text: Assesses the complete arrival-to-recipient path.
Identifies the downstream bottleneck possibility.
Retains connector/offload/local-distribution requirements under sea-basing.

acceptable_alternatives: A bottleneck or minimum-capacity explanation is acceptable without numerical rates.
error_conditions: Treats sea-basing as eliminating shore-access or distribution constraints.
questions.derivation_note: Combines the cited premises for this bounded staff consequence. The full source packet remains visible.

questions.title: Delivery-interface requirements
questions.question: What concrete logistics requirement should be established before confirming an over-the-shore relief package?
questions.expected_answer: Confirm the available ship-to-shore transport, offload/handling capability, landing-site suitability and onward distribution capacity for the intended relief destinations. Match load configuration and any breakbulk arrangements to those confirmed interfaces, rather than assuming a large shipload can pass unchanged to small craft or final recipients. Request unresolved connector/handling support before confirming throughput.

criteria.text: Requires confirmation of ship-to-shore connector capability.
Requires confirmation of offload/handling capability.
Requires destination and onward-distribution compatibility.
Requires load/breakbulk configuration matched to confirmed interfaces.

acceptable_alternatives: A joint logistics-over-the-shore capability/compatibility checklist is acceptable.
Breakbulk may be afloat or at an authorized staging point if justified by verified interfaces.
error_conditions: Invents a landing site or guaranteed JLOTS throughput.
questions.derivation_note: Combines the cited premises for this bounded staff consequence. The full source packet remains visible.

questions.title: Port operating-capacity requirement
questions.question: What current entry-point information should be requested to compare fixed-port and sea-based relief delivery?
questions.expected_answer: Request the operating status, usable handling/berthing or runway/ramp capacity, restrictions and restoration estimate for Bauerfield and Lapetasi, and the corresponding access/capacity status of any proposed alternative. Tie the response to the feasible relief-throughput comparison, not just an open/closed label.

criteria.text: Requests current Bauerfield operating status.
Requests usable Bauerfield handling/airfield capacity.
Requests current Lapetasi operating status.
Requests usable Lapetasi berthing/handling capacity.
Requests relevant operating restrictions.
Requests restoration timing.
Links the answer to the fixed-port versus alternative-throughput decision.

acceptable_alternatives: An FFIR, PIR or logistics information request is acceptable if the functional question is identical.
error_conditions: Assumes an open port has adequate throughput or approved access.

questions.title: Conditional port-restoration preparation
questions.question: What preparation is justified for Lapetasi while its usable throughput remains unresolved?
questions.expected_answer: Prepare a conditional survey/clearance and port-restoration support package for lead-agency validation, identifying the engineering/handling capability, assessment information and permissions required. Make execution contingent on host consent, tasking and validated need. Preparation does not establish that the US is authorized to open the port or that port opening is the fastest relief option.

criteria.text: Requires assessment/preparation of port-restoration support.
Keeps port-support execution conditional on the relevant consent/tasking.
Keeps port-support execution conditional on validated need.
Does not assume restoration feasibility or superiority before comparison.

acceptable_alternatives: A be-prepared support task or request for engineering assessment is acceptable.
error_conditions: Begins port opening under a blanket immediate-response exception.

questions.title: Need horizon and force horizon
questions.question: How do reported humanitarian urgency and full US force closure compare?
questions.expected_answer: The running estimate places acute needs in days but full force closure in weeks. Lift/sealift are shared and constrained by long distances. New Caledonia is about 500 km away, eastern Australia about 1,800 km and Guam about 4,000 nautical miles, but staging permissions are not pre-authorized.

criteria.text: States days for acute needs and weeks for full closure.
Identifies shared/time-phased lift.
Identifies relative distance to potential staging anchors.
Preserves unconfirmed staging permissions.

acceptable_alternatives: Relative distance is sufficient if the time mismatch is correct.
error_conditions: Invents exact arrival dates from distance alone.
questions.derivation_note: Retrieves the supplied scenario statement with its qualifications.

questions.title: Adequacy of waiting for full closure
questions.question: What does the mismatch between acute-needs timing and full force closure imply for an initial relief estimate?
questions.expected_answer: An estimate that starts useful relief only after full closure cannot be assumed to meet the early need window. Initial available capability and delivered benefit must be assessed separately from later scale. Nearby partner capability may reduce delay, but proximity alone does not establish permission, allocation or actual delivery time.

criteria.text: Identifies the mismatch with early needs.
Separates initial delivery from later full capacity.
Does not infer available support from proximity alone.

acceptable_alternatives: A phased capability-versus-need assessment is acceptable.
error_conditions: Assumes every acute need can wait until the complete force arrives.

questions.title: Phased delivery and closure information
questions.question: What information and evaluation measure should be used to assess the speed of a proposed relief package?
questions.expected_answer: Request confirmed dates and usable quantities for the initial and follow-on lift, sea-basing and support components. Measure time to the first useful delivery of the prioritized need at the affected destination, and subsequent sustainable throughput, rather than time to deployment order or arrival at a staging base. Identify the unmet early needs if confirmed capacity arrives too late.

criteria.text: Requests phased actual closure/capability confirmation.
Defines speed by useful delivery at the destination.
Separately identifies sustainable delivery throughput.
Identifies unmet needs within the early window.

acceptable_alternatives: Time to first effective support may be measured by service availability, such as a usable medical service, rather than cargo tonnage.
error_conditions: Reports a staging arrival as completed relief.

questions.title: Consent status and limits
questions.question: What does the packet establish about host-nation consent and political restrictions?
questions.expected_answer: Consent is contested and its authoritative locus unstable during caretaker political maneuvering. Some Port Vila/district access has been restricted. Deliberate restriction is assessed at moderate confidence as at least partly plausible, but administrative confusion has not been ruled out. No sovereign-territory activity may presume ungranted consent, and sea-based options do not authorize entry without it.

criteria.text: Identifies contested/unstable consent.
Preserves uncertainty about deliberate versus administrative restriction.
States the consent requirement for sovereign-territory activity.

acceptable_alternatives: Distinguish an international assistance request from clearance for a specific activity.
error_conditions: States that the Vanua Tasi bloc’s deliberate obstruction is conclusively established.
questions.derivation_note: Retrieves the supplied scenario statement with its qualifications.

questions.title: Sea-basing and consent
questions.question: How would denial of permission to use Port Vila affect the feasibility of a sea-based or outer-island relief option?
questions.expected_answer: It would remove or constrain that entry point, making alternatives relevant, but would not automatically authorize any other landing or distribution activity. Sea-basing can reduce fixed-port dependence; the receiving location still requires its own access/consent and delivery-feasibility assessment. A denial cannot be treated as permission to bypass sovereignty through another beach or island.

criteria.text: Identifies the effect on the denied entry point.
Distinguishes fixed-port independence from consent independence.
Requires location-specific assessment of the alternative.

acceptable_alternatives: Hold the affected ashore element while evaluating authorized alternatives.
error_conditions: Moves ashore elsewhere solely because Port Vila consent was denied.
questions.derivation_note: Combines the cited premises for this bounded staff consequence. The full source packet remains visible.

questions.title: Relief commitment decision gate
questions.question: What conditions should the staff place on committing relief ashore or through a sea-based alternative?
questions.expected_answer: Require current confirmation of consent/appropriate tasking for the specific receiving activity, usable end-to-end throughput and an acceptable incident-avoidance/force-protection arrangement. Record each condition independently. If a condition is unresolved, defer that activity and pursue clarification or another independently authorized option; do not force access or invoke a standing immediate-response workaround.

criteria.text: Requires activity-specific consent/tasking.
Requires usable throughput.
Requires incident-avoidance/force-protection readiness.
Gives a hold/review consequence for an unresolved gate.

acceptable_alternatives: A commit/hold/alternative decision matrix is acceptable.
error_conditions: Uses sea-basing or immediate-response language to bypass required consent.
questions.derivation_note: Combines the cited premises for this bounded staff consequence. The full source packet remains visible.

questions.title: Potential staging and partner support
questions.question: Which regional staging and partner capabilities are described, and what authorization is established?
questions.expected_answer: FRANZ comprises France, Australia and New Zealand. Australia has substantial regional lift including an LHD, helicopters and landing craft; New Zealand offers sealift, patrol, engineering and medical capability; France has regional aviation/engineering support at Nouméa. New Caledonia, Australia and Guam are potential staging anchors, but the packet does not pre-authorize basing, staging or overflight.

criteria.text: Identifies France, Australia and New Zealand as FRANZ.
Identifies the supplied broad partner capability differences.
Identifies the three potential staging anchors.
States that permissions are not pre-authorized.

acceptable_alternatives: Capability categories and location names suffice without exact force counts.
error_conditions: Treats Nouméa or Australian staging as already approved.

questions.title: Availability of a nearby staging option
questions.question: How should the staff compare a nearby potential staging location with a more distant established support location?
questions.expected_answer: Proximity reduces one distance but does not establish a usable support option. Approval, departure-point handling, actual lift allocation and onward delivery capacity must be considered with travel/closure time. A nearby unapproved or handling-limited point cannot automatically be credited as faster effective relief.

criteria.text: Separates geographic proximity from approval and capacity.
Includes departure handling and onward lift.
Compares time to useful relief rather than map distance alone.

acceptable_alternatives: A conditional comparison is acceptable without selecting a unique base.
error_conditions: Selects the closest site solely on distance.

questions.title: Staging decision and information request
questions.question: What should be obtained before selecting and timing requests for a staging arrangement?
questions.expected_answer: Obtain the relevant partners’ contribution and basing/overflight approvals, the operating status and handling throughput of candidate departure points, allocated lift and realistic closure/onward-delivery estimates. Compare authorized feasible options, including afloat support, and identify the decision/request deadline required by the early relief need. Do not prescribe a date or unique base absent those data.

criteria.text: Requests actual partner-contribution confirmation.
Requests relevant staging/basing approval.
Requests relevant overflight approval.
Requests departure-point operating status.
Requests departure-point handling throughput.
Requests actual lift/force-closure timing.
Links comparison/request timing to early delivery need.

acceptable_alternatives: An options-and-approvals matrix is acceptable.

questions.title: Civilian lead and humanitarian support rules
questions.question: What lead, validation and funding conditions govern the military relief contribution?
questions.expected_answer: USINDOPACOM is supported for DoD execution, while USAID/BHA DART leads the US disaster response and validates requests. The Chief of Mission leads consent diplomacy. DoD assistance is request-driven, time-bound, cost-reimbursable and limited to capability not reasonably available from civilian/host/international sources. Humanitarian principles and the UN cluster system govern coordination; direct military delivery is a last resort.

criteria.text: Distinguishes supported military command from civilian response lead.
States that support requires a validated request/tasking.
States the unique-capability/last-resort condition.
States the time-bound support limit.
States the cost-reimbursable support condition.
Identifies humanitarian/cluster coordination.
States direct military delivery is a last resort.

acceptable_alternatives: Use the source’s agency labels as scenario facts, without assumptions about current institutions.
error_conditions: Makes the joint force the lead disaster-response authority.
Treats military capacity as self-authorizing relief.

questions.title: Need for a military contribution
questions.question: How should the staff determine whether an available military capability addresses a valid relief gap?
questions.expected_answer: Availability is not enough. The intended need must be validated and compared with civilian, host, partner and other existing relief provision. Existing provision may be incomplete or inaccessible, so its nominal presence is not proof that the need is met either. The military contribution should fill a confirmed capability/time/location gap and remain accountable to the civilian-led process.

criteria.text: Separates military availability from validated unmet need.
Considers actual accessible existing provision.
Defines the contribution by a specific capability/time/location gap.

acceptable_alternatives: A needs-versus-provision matrix is acceptable.
error_conditions: Uses competitor presence alone to justify duplicating aid.

questions.title: Relief-provider capability register
questions.question: What information should the staff collect to support the unique-capability test?
questions.expected_answer: Through the lead agency and humanitarian coordination mechanism, establish who is providing which commodity/service, where, when and at usable capacity, including committed NGO/IGO, host and partner provision and available PRC relief services. Distinguish an announced commitment from delivered/accessible capacity. Use the register to identify validated gaps, not to rank providers by nationality.

criteria.text: Requests provider/service/location/time/capacity information.
Includes committed civilian/international and other existing relief.
Distinguishes announced from usable provision.

questions.title: Time-bounded support and transition record

questions.expected_answer: Record the validated need, tasking/consent, specific capability gap, supported location, authorized support period and reimbursement/accounting responsibility. Identify the civilian/host/partner capacity that would permit handover and a review condition for ending or adjusting military support. criteria.text: Records the validated assistance task.
Records its authorized support period.
Records accounting/reimbursement responsibility.

questions.title: Community access and coordination
questions.question: What local and humanitarian structures affect distribution beyond Port Vila?
questions.expected_answer: Customary chiefs have significant community-level authority, particularly on outer islands, and influence receipt and distribution. The UN cluster system and NGOs are established partners. Dispersed mountainous/coastal communities often require sea/air access, and permission for the capital does not establish access to every district.

Identifies UN clusters/NGOs.

questions.title: Value of partner and community interfaces
questions.question: How can regional and humanitarian relationships address gaps in a military-led picture of relief needs and receipt?
questions.expected_answer: FRANZ, humanitarian and customary-authority contacts can clarify local needs, reception and distribution constraints that a remote military picture may miss. These interfaces complement lift capability but do not automatically provide capacity or substitute for formal tasking/consent. Their value is in verified local coordination and needs assessment, not assumed universal acceptance.

criteria.text: Requests current affected-population locations.
Requests current population estimates.
Requests priority unmet needs.
Requests local receipt/distribution arrangements.
Requests relevant community acceptance or concerns.

questions.title: Medical situation and available categories
questions.question: What medical needs and support categories are reported?
questions.expected_answer: Acute trauma care, water/sanitation and disease-prevention needs are reported among displaced populations. Fixed ashore medical infrastructure is degraded. Afloat medical support is described as an offset; apportioned US maritime forces include medical capability and New Zealand offers medical detachments. Peace Ark is already conducting medical assistance, but no sufficient quantified capacity, accessibility or US hospital-ship commitment is supplied.

criteria.text: Identifies acute medical-care needs.

questions.question: What does the presence of a hospital ship or a planned medical detachment establish about whether affected communities’ medical needs can be met?
questions.expected_answer: It establishes a potential service source, not adequacy for all needs or locations. Type of care, usable capacity, access/referral arrangements and arrival/availability time must match the needs. Afloat care also does not by itself solve water, sanitation and prevention needs or transport between dispersed communities and the service.

criteria.text: Separates provider presence from adequate accessible coverage.
Requires care type/capacity/time and access matching.
Distinguishes hospital care from broader public-health/distribution needs.

criteria.text: Requests actual regional/afloat medical availability.

questions.question: What limits the establishment of relief coordination at the outset?
questions.expected_answer: Fixed communications on Efate are largely inoperative. Deployable/satellite communications are needed from the outset and are themselves lift-dependent. questions.title: PRC presence and conduct assessment
questions.question: What is reported and assessed about the PRC presence and permitted interaction?

Physical obstruction by force is assessed unlikely, while shadowing/visibility competition are plausible. US forces are directed to deconflict and avoid incidents, with force limited to the stated self-defense/designated-defense scope.

questions.expected_answer: Establish the responsible contact/command point and working communication channel, and request current relevant locations, activities and any reported change in posture that would affect the timing or incident risk of relief. questions.title: Relief purpose and legitimacy guidance
questions.question: What purposes and communication constraints should shape evaluation of the relief effort?
questions.expected_answer: The specified purpose is timely credible relief that supports the civilian-led response and affected-state sovereignty, followed by transition to civilian/UN/host authorities. The military should support FRANZ rather than appear unilateral. PRC messaging portrays US relief as militarized; the commander directs speed and legitimacy to be considered together, with humanitarian neutrality and incident avoidance preserved.

questions.title: Validity of competitor-based success measures
questions.question: How should a proposed success measure based on reducing PRC visibility be assessed against the supplied relief purpose?
questions.expected_answer: It is not sufficient as a military relief-success measure. Visibility can change without improving delivered assistance, affected-state acceptance or neutral treatment of needs. Measures should distinguish useful relief and credible civilian/partner-led conduct from competitive appearance. A faster unilateral activity that lacks consent can undermine the very acceptance required for the mission.

questions.title: Relief and credibility evaluation criteria
questions.question: What evaluation criteria should be used to compare relief proposals without making competition the outcome?
questions.expected_answer: Use time to effective assistance and unmet-need coverage, confirmed consent/civilian validation, local acceptance and maintenance of neutral need-based delivery, and incident/force-protection risk. Report trade-offs separately. Do not define success as displacing or discrediting another provider. Record what information would allow acceptance or neutrality to be assessed rather than declaring them from publicity alone.

questions.title: Coordinated factual relief communication
questions.question: What communication task follows from the need to demonstrate credible civilian-led relief while avoiding a competing military narrative?
questions.expected_answer: Coordinate factual updates with the civilian lead, affected-state authorities and France, Australia and New Zealand, identifying validated services, how people can access them and the partners’ support roles. Check statements against actual delivery and consent. Address inaccurate claims through verifiable facts while maintaining humanitarian neutrality, rather than use relief as a vehicle for discrediting another provider.

notes: All 107 accepted items were examined against the complete scenario packet. The resulting chains emphasize delivered relief, consent, feasible capacity, civilian validation and concrete coordination.
The sea-basing task is already explicitly in the sources, so R032 is retained as an A premise with its original accepted case preserved and a construction-stage correction recorded.
Several original organizational labels and medical-platform names are treated as acceptable exemplars rather than mandatory unique solutions. Functional equivalence is explicitly scored.
The original language requirement is operationalized as verifying actual working-language needs; no single invented Vanuatu language or fixed linguist quantity is assumed.
All new answers, criteria and links remain constructed proposals pending expert validation. No actual force availability, deployment, effect or experiment is claimed.

Final construction review separated independent factual/action conditions into atomic scoring entries. Additional authority, consent and recovery prerequisites enter the particular F tasks directly instead of being hidden behind a generic B answer. Companion questions are traced through source locators and chain ancestry rather than fabricated direct original-item mappings.
